notesStmt.note: It is possible that this manuscript was created in the days between the death of General Philip Sheridan on August 5, 1888, and the poem's publication on August 12, 1888. However, its unusually clean appearance and the existence of a different manuscript that seems obviously to have served as the printer's copy (see yal.00013) suggest that Whitman wrote the present manuscript out sometime after its initial publication, as a gift or at the request of an admirer.

This poem first appeared, without title, in the 12 August 1888 issue of the New York Herald, at the head of the paper's coverage of Sheridan's funeral. For its reprinting in Good-Bye My Fancy (1891), Whitman restored the title and added both a headnote and a footnoote.

lg.head: Interpolation Sounds.
lg.l: Over and through the burial chant,
Organ and solemn service, sermon, bending priests,

Of sudden battle's hurry and harsh noises—war's,
war's grim game to sight and ear in earnest;

The scout call'd up and forward—the General mounted,
and his aides around him—the new⹀brought
word—the instantaneous order issued,

The rifle crack—the cannon thud—the rushing
forth of men from their tents,

The clank of cavalry—the strange celerity of
forming ranks—the slender bugle note,

The sound of horses' hoofs departing—saddles,
arms, accoutrements.
